sheet-53.description: Sheet 53, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the southern end of the town between New York Avenue at the top and the Board Walk and the Atlantic Ocean at the foot. The title North Wildwood, formerly Anglesea, is lettered at the upper left. Numbered avenues, 26th to 19th, run across the sheet as paired West and East streets, with West 26th to West 19th above New Jersey Avenue and East 26th to East 19th below Central Avenue. New Jersey Avenue is a wide street carrying the double track of the W. J. & S. R. R. across the whole sheet; Central Avenue and Pennsylvania Avenue run parallel to it to the south. Philadelphia Avenue, Pacific Avenue and Atlantic Avenue are lettered at the left edge, outside the blocks, with the adjoining sheet numbers 48, 51 and 52 in the margin. Blocks are numbered 164 to 170, 195 to 201, 226 to 232 and 257 to 263, each divided into narrow lots with lot numbers. Most of the ground is vacant; the buildings are scattered frame dwellings, with a few outbuildings. The largest is the Wildwood Manor, a hotel of several wings close to the Board Walk, and The Greylock stands on Pennsylvania Avenue. A compass rose with a north arrow sits on New Jersey Avenue at the right. Four- and six-inch water pipes are drawn in the streets with a few hydrants, and the Board Walk is shown along the bottom with an approach at each street end and the Atlantic Ocean beyond. Streets are marked 70 ft wide.
notes: Pennsylvania Avenue is now Atlantic Avenue.
New Jersey Avenue here carries the W. J. & S. R. R. (Penn. R. R.) tracks; north of 1st Avenue it survives as Olde New Jersey Avenue.
Central Avenue south of 1st Avenue keeps its name (Central Avenue); north of 1st it is North Central Avenue.
Map, 100 ft. W./E. 26th to 19th Av, New York Av to the Boardwalk (New Jersey, Central, Pennsylvania Av). New Jersey Av carries the W.J.&S. R.R. tracks: left out. One part.

sheet-54.description: Sheet 54, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, continues the grid of sheet 53 to the east and covers the blocks between New York Avenue at the top and the Board Walk at the foot. West 19th to West 12th Avenues lie above New Jersey Avenue and East 19th to East 12th Avenues below Central Avenue, with blocks numbered 171 to 178, 202 to 209, 233 to 240 and 264 to 271. New Jersey Avenue crosses the sheet with the double track of the W. J. & S. R. R. (Penn. R. R.), and a compass rose with a north arrow sits on it at the upper right. Most blocks are vacant lots, with scattered dwellings. Near the middle of the sheet, beside the railroad, are the North Wildwood R.R. Station and a fire station with a chemical engine; boarding houses are marked in blocks 205 and 235. One building at East 19th Avenue is coloured pink. The Ottens, a large hotel of four and a half storeys, fronts the Board Walk at East 17th Avenue, and a small building marked vacant, to be removed, stands in the block beside it. The Board Walk, with its approaches, runs along the foot of the sheet, and Ottens Base Ball Park is drawn below it at the bottom edge, with vacant ground beyond. Water pipes of four and six inches are marked in the avenues. The scale bar is at the lower right.
notes: Pennsylvania Avenue is now Atlantic Avenue.
New Jersey Avenue here carries the W. J. & S. R. R. (Penn. R. R.) tracks; north of 1st Avenue it survives as Olde New Jersey Avenue.
Central Avenue south of 1st Avenue keeps its name (Central Avenue); north of 1st it is North Central Avenue.
Map, 100 ft. W./E. 19th to 12th Av, New York Av to the Boardwalk; North Wildwood R.R. station, The Ottens, Ottens Base Ball Park at the beach edge. New Jersey Av with tracks: left out. One part.

sheet-55.description: Sheet 55, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, shows the lowland west of the built-up town, where Otten's Canal cuts across the sheet from left to right. At the top, West 15th Avenue and West 16th Avenue run across the sheet, with West 17th Avenue below them, and West 19th Avenue at the foot; there is no West 18th Avenue label on this sheet. Virginia Avenue runs down the left of the middle blocks and Maryland Avenue down the right. The blocks, numbered 63 to 67, 88 to 92 and 113 to 117, are divided into long narrow lots running across from avenue to avenue. A tidal creek or arm of the canal, drawn in blue, enters from the upper left and widens into a basin, crossed by a foot bridge at the level of West 17th Avenue. The canal itself, lettered Otten's Canal, runs along the middle of the sheet, with a stepped basin on its south bank in which stand the Wildwood Yacht Club and a dwelling. North of the canal a boat builder's shop stands near an elevated water tank, and a boat house and dwellings stand on the Maryland Avenue side. Few other buildings are drawn, mostly dwellings with a few outbuildings. A compass rose with a north arrow stands on the vacant ground at the left, and a scale of feet is at the lower left. The streets are marked 70 ft wide, and six-inch water pipes are drawn in the avenues.
notes: Virginia Avenue is now Ohio Avenue; only the part south of the canal survives.
Otten's Canal has been filled in; Northwest 18th Avenue runs near its line today.

Map, 50 ft, turned 90 degrees (numbered avenues across the page). W. 15th to 19th Av, Virginia Av (now Ohio Avenue, south of the canal only) and Maryland Av; Otten's Canal, Wildwood Yacht Club. One part.

sheet-56.description: Sheet 56, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, lies east of sheet 55 and shows the area on both sides of Delaware Avenue where Otten's Canal ends. West 15th, 16th, 17th, 18th and 19th Avenues run across the sheet from left to right, and Delaware Avenue runs north to south through the middle; New York Avenue is lettered up the right edge. Blocks 113 to 117 lie west of Delaware Avenue and blocks 139 to 143 east of it, the eastern ones laid out in narrow lots with letters marking the buildings. The canal, lettered Otten's Canal, enters from the left and ends in a squared basin beside Delaware Avenue, where a landing is lettered along its eastern bank. On its north bank stand a boat house and a platform, with a long shed and small buildings on the west side of Delaware Avenue; a further dwelling stands on the south bank. East of Delaware Avenue the lots are largely vacant, with scattered dwellings, a carpenter's shop and a few outbuildings in blocks 140 and 141. A compass rose with a north arrow stands at the crossing of West 16th Avenue and Delaware Avenue. Six- and four-inch water pipes run in the avenues, with hydrants. A scale of feet is drawn at the lower right, and the sheet numbers 53, 54 and 55 are printed in the margins.
notes: Otten's Canal has been filled in; Northwest 18th Avenue runs near its line today.
Map, 50 ft, turned 90 degrees. W. 15th to 19th Av, Delaware Av to New York Av; east end of Otten's Canal. One part.

sheet-57-1.description: Sheet 57, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the centre of the old town of Anglesea, from New York Avenue at the top to Surf Avenue at the foot. West 8th to West 1st Avenues run across the sheet from left to right above New Jersey Avenue, and East 8th to East 1st Avenues below Central Avenue. Blocks 181 to 188, 211 to 219, 243 to 250 and 274 to 281 are drawn with their lot numbers. New Jersey Avenue carries the double track of the W. J. & S. R. R. (Penn. R. R.), which swings up to the right past the Anglesea Depot and a freight house. Near the depot stand the Hotel Germantown and the Hotel Hilton, and along the railroad on New Jersey Avenue are the Wildwood Water Works Co. pumping station with a stand pipe, E. E. Heil's coal and wood yard, the Arctic Ice Co. and the South Jersey Construction Co. cement block works. The Borough Hall, an M. E. Church, a Baptist Church, a club house and the Columbia Cottage are among the buildings south of Central Avenue, with many dwellings in the blocks nearest the inlet. Hereford Inlet appears at the lower right corner. An inset of the public school at the left edge is a separate part of this sheet. A compass rose with a north arrow stands near the left on New Jersey Avenue.
notes: Pennsylvania Avenue is now Atlantic Avenue.
New Jersey Avenue here carries the W. J. & S. R. R. (Penn. R. R.) tracks; north of 1st Avenue it survives as Olde New Jersey Avenue.
Central Avenue south of 1st Avenue keeps its name (Central Avenue); north of 1st it is North Central Avenue.

Map, 100 ft. W./E. 8th to 1st Av, New York Av to Surf Av; Anglesea depot, water works. Part 2: boxed inset at left (North Wildwood Public School, block 211, E. 9th Av and Central Av), one block south-west of where it is drawn.

sheet-57-2.description: This boxed inset at the left edge of sheet 57, drawn at 100 ft to an inch like the rest of the sheet, shows the North Wildwood Public School at the corner of East 9th Avenue and Central Avenue. It is drawn inside a heavy double border and has its own block numbers, 211 and 212, with the lot numbers of the blocks printed beside them. East 9th Avenue runs vertically through the inset and Central Avenue is lettered along its foot. The school is a pink-coloured building of two storeys with projecting wings, lettered North Wildwood Public School, with a note that it is heated by hot air and has no lights. The remark No Exposure Any Side is printed above it. A six-inch water pipe is drawn along Central Avenue and a hydrant stands at the corner. Beside it, the inset shows parts of blocks 212 and 213 to the east of East 9th Avenue, with lot lines and numbers, and no other buildings are drawn. Streets are marked 70 ft and 100 ft wide.
notes: Central Avenue at E. 9th Avenue keeps its name today (Central Avenue).
The inset shows the corner one block south-west of where it is drawn on the sheet.

Map, 100 ft. W./E. 8th to 1st Av, New York Av to Surf Av; Anglesea depot, water works. Part 2: boxed inset at left (North Wildwood Public School, block 211, E. 9th Av and Central Av), one block south-west of where it is drawn.

sheet-58-1.description: Sheet 58, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, shows the northern end of the town beside Hereford Inlet, a broad tidal channel drawn in blue that runs diagonally from the lower left to the top. The main part covers the area from North Central Avenue at the top to North Surf Avenue at the foot, with Pennsylvania Avenue crossing it twice. 1st Avenue is lettered at the left edge, Chestnut Avenue and Walnut Avenue run up the middle, and Spruce Avenue and Park Avenue lie to the right. At the top left the blocks 251 and 252 hold the U. S. Life Saving Station with its boat house, an oil house and sheds, and the U. S. Light House stands in the lower part of block 251. The inlet cuts through these blocks and across block 282 below, leaving some lots partly under water. Blocks 253 and 287 are laid out but unbuilt, and block 283 lies below. A compass rose with a north arrow stands at the right. The sheet numbers 57 and 59 are printed in the margins. A boxed inset of the Hereford Fishing and Gunning Club in the lower right belongs to another part of the sheet and is not described here. Four- and six-inch water pipes are marked near the left edge.
notes: North Central Avenue appears here with the sheet number 59 printed over its name.
Pennsylvania Avenue is now Atlantic Avenue.
Modern Surf Avenue north of 1st Avenue does not follow the drawn N. Surf Avenue (about 10 m off); not used as control.

Map, 50 ft. Anglesea north end: 1st Av to Spruce Av, N. Central Av to N. Surf Av; U.S. Life Saving Station, U.S. Light House, Hereford Inlet. Pennsylvania Av drawn at two positions (jog at Chestnut Av). Part 2: boxed inset of the Hereford Fishing & Gunning Club, 1/2 mile north of Anglesea P.O., salt marsh, no streets.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Hereford Fishing & Gunning Club and Arctic Fishing Club, salt marsh, 1/2 mile north of Anglesea P.O. (no street junction or feature shared with modern data or another sheet).

sheet-59.description: Sheet 59, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, shows the built-up streets between New York Avenue at the top and North Central Avenue at the foot, west of Hereford Inlet. New Jersey Avenue runs across the middle, with the W. J. & S. R. R. (Penn. R. R.) double track sweeping diagonally from the lower left to the top centre. From left to right 1st Avenue, Chestnut Avenue, Walnut Avenue and Spruce Avenue cross the sheet, framing blocks 189 to 192 and 220 to 223. The inlet, in blue, runs along the right edge and cuts diagonally across the lower right, with a platform and pier built on piles at its crossing. The blocks along New Jersey Avenue hold most of the buildings: Hotel Scott, a restaurant and Hotel 2nd, stores and offices at the left, the Rosewood, Walnut Ave. Hotel and the Hereford Hotel in the middle, and the Hotel Royal with a beer garden, boarding houses and a club house in block 222. At the right a moving picture house and shops stand at the inlet shore. A vacant school house is drawn at the lower left, and dwellings fill the blocks near Chestnut Avenue. Sheet numbers 57, 58 and 60 are printed in the margins, and water pipes of four and six inches run in the streets with hydrants. A compass rose and a scale of feet are drawn on the sheet.
notes: The railroad diagonal here is now West Anglesea Drive.
New Jersey Avenue north of 1st Avenue survives as Olde New Jersey Avenue; New York Avenue is now North New York Avenue; North Central Avenue keeps its name.
Map, 50 ft. Anglesea: 1st Av to Spruce Av, New York Av to N. Central Av; hotels (Scott, Hereford, Royal, Walnut Ave), W.J.&S. R.R. diagonal (now West Anglesea Drive, not used). One part.

sheet-60.description: Sheet 60, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the upper end of the town on the edge of the marsh, from Maryland Avenue at the top to New York Avenue at the foot. Delaware Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet, and 2nd Avenue, 1st Avenue, Chestnut Avenue, Walnut Avenue and Spruce Avenue run down it from the left to the right, marked 70 ft wide where lettered. A creek, lettered Beach Creek, winds from the lower left to the top through the marsh, which is lettered Marsh Land and left blank in the upper left corner, and cuts through blocks 126, 127 and 128. Blocks 157 to 160 below Delaware Avenue are drawn with long lot lines and mostly vacant. The few buildings are dwellings, a club house at the creek, a row of small houses in block 128, a shed, a vacant building and a tar pot among the lots at Walnut Avenue. At the lower right the railroad (W. J. & S. R. R., Penn. R. R.) crosses diagonally with a platform, the Fish Depot and other buildings. A compass rose with a north arrow stands in the upper left. Water pipes of four and six inches run in the streets. Sheet numbers 57 and 59 are printed in the margins, with a scale of feet at the lower left.
notes: The railroad diagonal here is now West Anglesea Drive.
New York Avenue is now North New York Avenue.
Map, 50 ft. Anglesea bay side: 2nd Av to Spruce Av, Maryland Av to New York Av; Beach Creek, marsh land, fish depot on the railroad. One part.
